trust_decision.summary: The daemon must not persist a client-supplied file unless its body is under a size cap and its content is proven decodable audio; the decision is made server-side at the HTTP layer (extension allow-list + GStreamer pbutils probe in the upload handler, plus a new ASGI body-size middleware) before anything is written to /tmp/reachy_mini_sounds.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the sound upload; upload_sound() is the only handler that writes a client-chosen filename plus client bytes to disk, and at the pinned commit it does so with only a path-traversal guard and no type, content or size check (media.py:160-175).

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/media/sounds/upload (HTTP, media router mounted under /api at src/reachy_mini/daemon/app/main.py:244,258)
new MaxBodySizeMiddleware, registered in create_app() from main.py
is_valid_audio_file(), called from the upload handler via asyncio.to_thread
examples/sound_play.py CLI: --wav replaced by --file plus audio_duration_seconds()

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/reachy_mini/daemon/backend/abstract.py:1575-1612 (_handle_audio_finish writes client base64 bytes as <upload_id>.wav under tempfile/reachy-mini-uploads/audio)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The chunked audio attachment is a separate recorded-move feature used by the TS SDK, the file is always named '<upload_id>.wav' so no dangerous extension reaches disk, and the only consumer is GStreamer playbin, so the advisory's multipart sounds-upload endpoint does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate playback of any decodable container, not just WAV: the SDK upload path posts whatever local file the caller hands to play_sound() and the daemon decodes it with GStreamer playbin, so an over-broad fix that allow-lists only .wav (or rejects anything the suffix says is not .wav) breaks working OGG/MP3/FLAC playback; the same handler also promises that re-uploading the same name overwrites in place.

O6_input_shapes: filename with directory prefix ('../../../tmp/evil.wav', '/etc/passwd') reduced to its basename
uppercase or mixed-case extension (.WAV) via Path(filename).suffix.lower()
disallowed extension (.sh) rejected before touching disk
allowed extension with non-audio content (probe with GstPbutils Discoverer)
oversized body with an honest Content-Length rejected before the body is read (413)
oversized body with absent or understated Content-Length / chunked transfer, aborted while streaming
multi-megabyte body read in 1 MiB chunks into a temp file instead of one read()

O7_producer.where: src/reachy_mini/io/protocol.py:488-548 (UploadAudioStartCmd/UploadAudioChunkCmd/UploadAudioFinishCmd: the only constraints are total_chunks<=16384 and chunk<=16 KiB; upload_id is an unconstrained str)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SDK WebSocket command upload_audio_start/chunk/finish assembles base64 chunks in memory and writes the decoded bytes to a .wav file with no content probe and no byte cap tied to MAX_SOUND_UPLOAD_BYTES
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the recorded-move audio attachment path, a different feature from sound upload, the name is forced to .wav and playbin silently fails on non-audio, so the advisory's endpoint-level protection looks inapplicable.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 package and 2 files from the landing point (daemon/app/routers -> io -> daemon/backend); the route is additionally reached from a second transport

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WebRTC data-channel command handler validates JSON with command_adapter and dispatches the same upload_audio_* commands, so no HTTP middleware (and therefore no size cap) is on the path at all
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: WebRTC peers are treated as paired/trusted clients and the new cap is an HTTP-layer control, so a solver can argue the data channel is out of the fix's layer.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the second implementation, 2 packages from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The client-chosen upload_id is interpolated straight into the destination path (f'{cmd.upload_id}.wav'), so a '../' upload_id escapes the audio temp dir; there is no basename/normalisation guard like media.py:164
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: upload_id is documented as a client-generated UUID, so a solver reads the traversal as impossible by contract rather than as an unchecked input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: inside the O2 second implementation, 2 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second upload route in the same router (e.g. /media/images/upload or a recording upload) reusing SOUNDS_TMP_DIR or a sibling temp dir with the same 'write client filename' shape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler is the obvious template to copy; a maintainer adding another client-to-daemon file transfer would clone it and reuse the traversal guard without the new type/content/size checks.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a body-size cap that must be registered for every upload path (the middleware keys on an exact frozenset of paths)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cap lives in an ASGI middleware registered in create_app with a hardcoded path set; adding an endpoint in another router silently leaves it uncapped unless the set is edited too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a persisted sibling of the move upload (assembled move JSON written to disk next to the audio file) with the same missing validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Move and audio upload slots are deliberately parallel implementations in the same class; a maintainer extending either one would mirror the other's (absent) validation.

O9_family: CWE-434 unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type / missing validation before writing client-supplied bytes to disk

O10_build.language: Python (>=3.10), plus a TypeScript SDK under ts/
O10_build.toolchain: setuptools build backend, pip or uv install of src/; pytest (testpaths=tests/unit_tests) with ruff/mypy in the dev group
O10_build.project_tests: pytest unit suite; the media area has tests/unit_tests/test_media_backend.py, test_media_server_watchdog.py, test_audio_gstreamer.py, but no tests for the sounds-upload route at the pinned commit (tests/unit_tests/test_media_upload_api.py is added by the fix, and its content-validation cases skip without GStreamer).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an extension allow-list (usually just .wav) inside upload_sound() in media.py and stop there, leaving the body cap unwired, the content probe out, and the SDK/WebRTC chunked audio path untouched.
